answer: Each identity runs a canyon photometer at a canyon inlet, locks a 70-credit bond, and files one nebula brightness reading per epoch, signed by its serial. An auditor recomputes it from the nebula brightness catalogue for that inlet; a reading off by over 0.1 magnitude or a reused serial burns the bond. The first filing costs 34, the kth costs 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028 and 1000 fakes pay 3031000 plus 70000 locked, as one photometer yields one reading per window. A rented-photometer ring fails on a shared serial. An honest operator files once for 34 and recovers the bond.
